summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in UC mucosa is a neutrophil-recruitment axis. CXCR2, CXCR1 and CXCL8 take the first three places of the convergence ranking, CXCR2 and CXCL8 are up in all eight cohorts, but single-cell data place almost all CXCR2 transcripts in neutrophils [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965] and most CXCL8 transcripts too [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873], so their bulk rise mainly reports neutrophil arrival rather than a change of the tissue itself.

Human genetics separates causes from consequences. IL12B has the top Open Targets association with UC and is the leading plasma Mendelian randomisation result: genetically higher protein raises UC risk [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539], so inhibition is the protective direction, as the UC drugs listed for it in the clinical-indications record (mirikizumab, guselkumab, risankizumab) agree. For CD274 (PD-L1) genetics points the other way: higher plasma protein lowers UC risk [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595].

Inside the tissue, DUOX2 in enterocytes and MMP1 in inflammatory fibroblasts keep a clear increase after the composition adjustment ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161] and [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]) and their cell source replicates across the single-cell atlases, while the epithelial gene AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss of the meta-analysis [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.7633] and HMGCS2 is among the largest losses.

Baseline CXCR2, CXCL8, TREM1 and IL11 are higher in ustekinumab non-responders, but each also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders, so they mark disease severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism; baseline IL23A, the target ustekinumab blocks, does not stratify its response [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977].

expression.text: The largest and most consistent increases in UC mucosa are remodelling, antimicrobial and neutrophil genes. CHI3L1 [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913] and MMP3 [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.822] are among the largest pooled increases of all genes up in the eight-cohort meta-analysis, and DUOX2 [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.3033] and CXCL8 [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687] are also up in all eight cohorts.

Epithelial metabolism is lost. AQP8 has the largest pooled loss of all genes down in the meta-analysis [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.7633] and falls in all eight cohorts, and HMGCS2 is among the largest losses. The loss of the epithelial transporter SLC26A2 stays significant after composition adjustment [gene=SLC26A2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-1.4638], a change of the tissue itself.

JAK2 is up in all eight cohorts but only modestly [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.833]; it has the second highest Open Targets association with UC, so its place among the candidates comes from genetics and drug history rather than expression.

inflammation.text: Most leading changes are local to inflamed mucosa. Comparing inflamed with non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients (GSE193677), CXCR2 rises [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972] with only a small change in non-inflamed versus control mucosa [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]; CD274 behaves the same way ([gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.0008] against [gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.1971]), and HMGCS2 is unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649], so its loss belongs to inflammation.
MMP3, DUOX2, TREM1 and AQP9 are also higher in inflamed than in non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients.

replication.text: The leading changes reproduce across cohorts: CXCR2, CHI3L1, DUOX2, JAK2 and AQP8 are significant in the same direction in all eight cohorts. At protein level, in an independent proteomics study, IDO1 [gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917] and HMGCS2 [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094] change in the same direction as RNA, whereas CHI3L1 rises much less as protein [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607] and was not called significant by the authors.

literature.text: Published support is thinner than the expression signal for the top candidates. CXCR2 has no verbatim-checked relation in the corpus; a Mendelian randomisation, colocalisation and transcriptomic study proposes CXCR1 and CXCR2 as neutrophil extracellular trap-related treatment targets in UC, and another ties the CXCL5 to CXCR2 axis to neutrophil chemotaxis. The cited IDO1 support is one experimental study: IDO1 was elevated in UC patients and colitis mice, drove pro-inflammatory macrophage polarisation through the GRP78-XBP1 pathway, and an IDO1 inhibitor ameliorated DSS colitis.

For biomarkers the literature is more useful. MMP1 is among the transcripts modified by mirikizumab that correlate with the modified Mayo score, Geboes score and Robarts Histopathology Index; CHI3L1 is upregulated in UC and promotes macrophage pyroptosis through BCAT1 and NF-kappaB; DUOX2 protein is among the most elevated in inflamed UC biopsies; and HMGCS2 is reported decreased in UC.

The CXCL8 axis with its receptors is described as taking part in UC pathogenesis through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signalling, and in a blood RNA-seq validation set CXCL8 was among the best diagnostic genes for IBD, second to ITGA5, an IBD-level rather than UC-specific result. CXCL1 is nominated as a diagnostic or activity marker in several bioinformatic studies; alone it is only a fair activity marker, and its high accuracy comes within a combined multi-gene model.

external.text: Approved-target genetics behaves as a positive control. IL12B has the top Open Targets association with UC and is the leading plasma Mendelian randomisation result: genetically higher protein raises UC risk [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539], the signal colocalises with an IBD GWAS locus and replicates in FinnGen, so inhibition is the protective direction.

Among expression-led candidates, genetics often points the other way. For CD274 higher plasma protein lowers UC risk [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595] although it rises in inflamed mucosa, which suggests a compensatory rise. CXCL5 is also protective in plasma [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634] but rests on a tag variant without colocalisation. SLC26A3 falls in inflamed mucosa, yet higher expression in IBDverse crypt progenitors raises UC risk [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]. CXCL8 is null in plasma (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]) and has no Open Targets genetic association.

CXCR2 has a high Open Targets genetic association score but no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so Mendelian randomisation could not test it. Reparixin (phase 3) and navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682, danirixin and elubrixin (phase 2) are recorded CXCR2 antagonists, none for UC. Mouse colitis papers include a selective antagonist that ameliorated acute colitis, but MGI has no single-gene colitis phenotype for it.

cells.text: Neutrophil genes lead the ranking but report cell arrival. In Gubatan 2026 neutrophils make most CXCR2 [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965], CXCL8 [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873] and TREM1 [gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894] transcripts, and the Smillie 2019 attribution of CXCR2 to T/NK cells does not replicate in the other atlases. After composition adjustment CXCL8 loses significance (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0525]) and CXCR2 keeps only a small change [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409].

Two increases are changes of the tissue itself. DUOX2 is made by enterocytes [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947] and MMP1 by inflammatory fibroblasts [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]; both attributions replicate in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122, and both keep a clear adjusted change ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161] and [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]). The loss of SLC26A2 is intrinsic [gene=SLC26A2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-1.4638], with almost no neutrophil contribution [gene=SLC26A2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.014].

IDO1, CHI3L1 and CD274 have mixed sources. IDO1 is myeloid in Smillie 2019 but epithelial in Gubatan 2026; CHI3L1 is stromal in Smillie 2019 but myeloid in Gubatan 2026, where neutrophils also contribute [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.466]; CD274 is myeloid-dominant but diffuse, with a large neutrophil share [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]. All three keep a significant change after adjustment ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505], [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967], [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]); the composition model can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so these are partly tissue changes.

spatial.text: In deconvolved Visium spots inflammatory fibroblasts give the largest in-situ contribution to MMP1 [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.568], and the spots with high MMP1 are enriched in inflammatory fibroblasts and neutrophils around them, so tissue and single-cell data agree. CosMx detects MMP1 only at background.
DUOX2 is placed in epithelium by both Xenium and Visium, in agreement with its enterocyte source in the single-cell atlases.

pathways.text: Pathway activity rises broadly in inflamed mucosa. NFkB and TNFa activity are up in all eight cohorts, the NFkB t reaching [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=18.79] in GSE206285, and JAK-STAT, TGFb, EGFR, MAPK, PI3K and Hypoxia are also up in all eight, WNT in seven. STAT3 regulon activity is up in all eight cohorts [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6], as is AP1. Because so many pathways rise together these signals are robust but not specific, and VEGF and Androgen are not consistent across cohorts.

The most specific circuit is neutrophil CXCL8 to CXCR2: in Gubatan 2026 the link from the Neutrophil CXCR4 state to the Neutrophil state rose strongly in inflamed mucosa, a feed-forward recruitment loop, and neutrophil CXCL8 also reaches ACKR1 endothelium. Inflammatory fibroblasts send CXCL1 to CXCR2 on neutrophils at much lower scores, IL1B mainly reaches the decoy receptor IL1R2 on neutrophil states, and the expected neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit is weak. Co-expression is not proof of signalling.

Of the circuit genes, CXCR2 has recorded antagonists (reparixin, navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682), IL1B has canakinumab, recorded as approved, and TREM1 has nangibotide in phase 2; no drug is recorded for CXCL1 or CXCL5.

treatment.text: Gene-level non-response signals are severity markers. Higher baseline CXCR2 (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]), CXCL8 ([gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]), TREM1 ([gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) and IL11 ([gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]) are associated with ustekinumab non-response, but each also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders ([gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126], [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154], [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234], [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]). OSM ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) is not significant in the UNIFI placebo arm ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), yet the drug-by-placebo interaction is not significant either ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.974]), so drug specificity is not shown.

At pathway level TNFa is higher in ustekinumab non-responders ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and in several other arms including UNIFI placebo, so it is a severity axis; it is not significant in PURSUIT placebo ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]) or the PROTECT mesalazine arm ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.5-ASA (PROTECT).padj=0.414]). TGFb behaves the same ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]; UNIFI placebo [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]). Target expression does not stratify response: IL23A for ustekinumab ([gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]) and ITGB7 for vedolizumab ([gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]). In the adalimumab single-cell atlas CXCL8 shows no baseline difference between remitters and non-remitters.

discovery.text: CHRDL2 has the largest pooled increase of the first-in-class candidates of the discovery screen and is up in [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=7] cohorts. Its transcripts are stromal, mostly inflammatory fibroblasts, and the other single-cell atlases agree [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; other_atlases_agreeing=3]. The increase is partly composition, an antibody is the predicted modality, and no response or functional data exist.

CPXM1 has the second largest increase of the first-in-class candidates. It is stromal in Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122 but epithelial in Gubatan 2026, its increase is partly composition, and genetics and response data are missing.

XKR9 keeps the highest share of its change after composition adjustment among the first-in-class candidates and is one of four epithelial candidates classed intrinsic, but it is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts, the second fewest of the candidates, and lacks response and functional evidence.

integration.text: The streams agree on a core picture. Expression, the paired inflamed and non-inflamed data, the pathway layer and single cells point to a neutrophil-rich inflamed mucosa with NFkB, TNFa and STAT3 activity and loss of epithelial metabolism, and the treatment data show that the same neutrophil signals mark severity in drug and placebo arms alike. Genetics and drug history agree for the positive controls IL12B and JAK2, which have the two highest Open Targets associations with UC.

They disagree on causality. CXCL8 and CHI3L1, among the strongest expression changes, have no Open Targets genetic association, and CXCL8 is null in plasma Mendelian randomisation, so they read as consequences of inflammation and as biomarkers. For CD274 and CXCL5 genetics runs opposite to an inhibitor, since higher plasma protein lowers risk, and for SLC26A3 the gut eQTL direction is opposite to its loss in biopsies. CXCR2 cannot be tested by Mendelian randomisation, so its causal direction is open.

targets.rationale: Positive control: it has the top Open Targets association with UC and is the leading plasma Mendelian randomisation result, with genetically higher protein raising UC risk [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539], colocalisation and FinnGen replication; the clinical-indications record lists UC drugs for it.

First in the convergence ranking and up in all eight cohorts, but neutrophils make almost all of its transcripts [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965] and only a small change survives composition adjustment [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]: a neutrophil-recruitment target, with clinical-stage antagonists recorded, and a severity marker that also separates placebo non-responders.

Placed above higher-ranked neutrophil genes because it is a change of the tissue itself: inflammatory fibroblasts make it [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871], Visium places it in the same cells [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.568], it keeps an adjusted change [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636], and it is among the transcripts modified by mirikizumab that track disease activity.

Enterocyte-derived [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], retained after composition adjustment [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161], placed in epithelium by Xenium and Visium and among the most elevated proteins in inflamed biopsies: a tissue biomarker of epithelial antimicrobial stress, with no drug recorded.

Positive control: second highest Open Targets association with UC and a UC drug listed in the clinical-indications record (upadacitinib), with only a modest expression change [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.833].

High in the convergence ranking and up in inflamed mucosa, but genetically higher plasma PD-L1 lowers UC risk [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595], so inhibition runs against genetics; its rise is best read as a compensatory response.

Up in all eight cohorts [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687], but made mostly by neutrophils and myeloid cells, it loses significance after composition adjustment (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0525]), is null in plasma Mendelian randomisation and marks severity in drug and placebo arms alike.

One of the largest pooled RNA increases [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913], retained after adjustment [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967], but the protein change is small [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607] and it has no Open Targets genetic association: a strong tissue biomarker, with targeting only exploratory.

Up in all eight cohorts and replicated as protein [gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917], with a mixed myeloid and epithelial source and an adjusted change [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]; the cited mechanism and inhibitor data come from one study in UC patients and colitis mice, so it is an interferon-response biomarker and at most a repurposing hypothesis.

Made mostly by neutrophils and myeloid cells [gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894], higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa and associated with ustekinumab non-response and placebo non-response alike; nangibotide is recorded in phase 2.

Falls in inflamed mucosa, but higher expression in crypt progenitors raises UC risk [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607], among the strongest colocalising gut eQTL results: the loss in disease may be a response, and the gene is a marker of epithelial transport rather than a target.
Up in all eight cohorts and made mostly by neutrophils, with part of the change retained after adjustment: a tissue marker of neutrophil influx.

Exploratory: the largest pooled increase of the first-in-class candidates, up in [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=7] cohorts, made by stromal cells (mostly inflammatory fibroblasts in Smillie 2019), a lineage all four atlases agree on, and antibody-tractable; partly composition, with no response or functional data.

Exploratory: the highest retained share after composition adjustment among the first-in-class candidates and an epithelial lineage, but up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts and without response or functional evidence.

limitations.text: Bulk changes of neutrophil and myeloid genes are confounded by cell influx; the composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so retained fractions are approximate.
Co-expression of ligand and receptor in single cells is not proof of signalling.
Several leading candidates (CXCR2, CXCR1, JAK2) have no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so their causal direction is untested rather than refuted.

Literature support rests on a few verbatim-checked sentences per gene from a local corpus; the CD274 hub-gene finding of the literature specialist was dropped because its citations are not linked to the gene.
A reading subagent checked every claim against its cited records; claims it found unsupported are listed in the Agents tab rather than removed.
